answer: An agent selling wharf safety alerts must lock collateral for each report until an independent inspection window closes. A false alert can cause a ripple of canceled bookings, so set the bond above the maximum fraud gain divided by the audit probability. Select audits after reports are committed and use evidence outside the reporter's control. Every alias must fund separate collateral, and proven lies forfeit it. A spiral of fake accounts then multiplies locked capital and expected losses. The deterrent relies on reliable inspections and enforceable penalties.
